coordinates: 1-based; end is exclusive. A span is maskable only when the parsed function body is wholly and positively established as ordinary Serene construction and a recognized execution path.
designRisks: Never mask a whole function because it contains one ordinary sql tag or bind call. Retain the whole function when any statement, call target, receiver, sink, or provenance is unresolved.
Do not infer spans from source comments, SQL string contents, names, or marker-shaped text. Use parser-derived function ranges from the exact source revision.
A parse failure invalidates every proposed mask in that file; preserve the raw matches and source for review.
Only parser-derived ranges may be compacted. Same-line functions require exact columns so a neighboring actionable function cannot be erased.

maskableSpans.why: The body constructs a fixed sql template, binds named values, and passes the bound text and values to a direct recognized query call.

nonmaskableSpans.why: One ordinary query does not make the body ordinary: the second query concatenates runtime term into SQL. The complete function must remain visible.
The unrecognized buildAuditTag call is unknown code in the same body. Broad function masking must not hide it, even though its result is not SQL text here.
The Serene value is sent through an unsupported opaqueGateway sink, so execution provenance cannot be positively established.
db[method](...) has a computed, runtime-selected call target. It cannot be upgraded to an ordinary recognized execution path.
The missing closing parenthesis makes the source unparsable. No lexical resemblance to ordinary Serene code may produce a mask.

maskableSpans.why: This function is independently a complete fixed-template, bound-value, direct-query path.

nonmaskableSpans.why: The neighboring function concatenates name into SQL and must remain visible.

maskableSpans.why: The function is ordinary despite the marker-shaped SQL string literal; classification and boundaries must come from parsed code, not text markers.

nonmaskableSpans.why: The adjacent same-line function concatenates runtime name into SQL. Exact parser-derived columns prevent its removal with the preceding function.
